reconcile.connective: The leading harmonization identifies Mosera with the desert of Mount Hor itself, so the two place-names mark one death-site, not two.

discrepancy.connective: Steven DiMattei presses the sharpest objection, arguing that Hor and Moserah are two genuinely contradictory death-traditions from rival priestly sources, only later stitched together.

skeptic.name: Steven DiMattei
skeptic.work: Contradictions in the Bible (contradictionsinthebible.com), “Where/When Did Aaron Die?”
skeptic.attribution: Steven DiMattei, Contradictions in the Bible (contradictionsinthebible.com, 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: Aben Ezra is of opinion, that Beeroth Benejaakan, or the wells of the children of Jaakan, is not the same with Bene Jaakan, nor Mosera the same with Moseroth; but Beeroth is Kadesh, and Mosera is the name of the desert of Mount Hor … it is certain that Aaron died on Mount Hor, Num 20:23, or there died and was buried when in the desert of Mosera …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes the Hor-vs-Moserah geography by identifying Mosera with the desert of Mount Hor, so the same site bears both names. The two clauses are non-adjacent in the note but the ellipsis join preserves Gill's sense (Mosera = desert of Mount Hor, hence Aaron died both 'on Mount Hor' and 'in the desert of Mosera').

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Deuteronomy 10:6
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, reconciling the death-site by identifying Mosera with the desert of Mount Hor (citing Aben Ezra) and by appeal to the back-and-forth marches between the stations.
